style: Style: an original illustration in the manner of a 17th–18th-century European copperplate engraving from an early travel book about Siam: fine sepia ink line work with careful cross-hatching and stippling for shading, monochrome brown-black ink on aged cream laid paper with foxing. Head-and-shoulders bust, three-quarter view, centred, facing slightly left, dignified and respectful. Plain aged-paper background fading to the edges, no scenery. Historically plausible late-18th-century Siamese dress and hairstyle (short-cropped mahat-thai hair). Not photorealistic, not anime, not a game character. No text, no letters, no captions, no seals, no signature, no border.

items.taksin_b: Phraya Tak (later King Taksin) at about 33, a Siamese general of Thai-Chinese (Teochew) descent: lean, determined face, calm resolute eyes, short-cropped hair, thin moustache; wearing a fitted long-sleeved Siamese noble's military jacket with an embroidered collar over a sash, a sword hilt at the shoulder.
